question: The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) is the largest provider of humanitarian aid to Palestinian refugees living in the Gaza Strip, the West Bank, Syria, Lebanon and Jordan. Over 5.9 million Palestinians are registered with the agency and over 50 % of its regular budget is dedicated to education.

Since the resumption of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict last October, the humanitarian situation of Palestinian citizens has dramatically deteriorated and became critical in terms of food insecurity and malnutrition, according to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification.

However, after the recent accusations against 12 UNRWA employees for taking part in the Hamas-led October 7 attack, several European countries decided to withdraw their financial assistance to the UNRWA.

While the UN took the allegations very seriously and reacted immediately, organizations such as HRW and DWB warn that a suspension of funding to UNRWA will have devastating consequences and that a further cut in food, water and medicine supplies might lead to famine. 1.
What measures does the Commission plan to take in response to Palestinians’ critical food situation, limited access to water and shelter troubles?
How does the Commission plan to ensure EU’s support for UNRWA?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.7.2024) On 1 March 2024, the Commission announced its decision to allocate an additional EUR 68 million to support the Palestinian population across the region to be implemented through international partners like the Red Cross and the Red Crescent1.

This comes on top of the allocated EUR 125 million of humanitarian aid for Palestinians for 2024, of which the Commission contracted the first EUR 16 million on 1 March 2024 for food, medical and nonfood items, shelter, as well as education and psycho-social support to civilians in Gaza.

Furthermore, the Commission has engaged with the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA)’s Commissioner General and welcomed his commitment to tackle the serious issues at stake, linked to accusations against 12 UNRWA employees.
Letters outlining the way forward with all the measures and procedures for the Commission’s conditional funding for UNRWA were exchanged on 1 and 6 March 2024.

The conditions for the disbursement of the first tranche were the following: agreement by UNRWA on the three workstreams (the screening of UNRWA staff; system audit; reinforcement of the Department of Internal Investigations and Ethics office) and the signature of the EU-UNRWA contribution agreement; declaration in writing by UNRWA that up-to-date, necessary and proportionate information on staff has been shared and will be done on a quarterly basis; and the adoption by UNRWA of a concept note detailing how to strengthen Department of Internal Oversight Services and Ethics office.

Following UNRWA’s fulfilment of these conditions, the Commission paid a first tranche of EUR 50 million out of the EUR 82 million foreseen for UNRWA for 2024. The second and third tranches of EUR 16 million are subject to the implementation of the agreement with UNRWA and the Agency’s compliance with the agreed conditions and milestones.
